questions.question: Explain the significance of withdrawal symptoms in diagnosis of dependence. / Part D
questions.solution_html:
• Withdrawal Symptoms
  • Withdrawal occurs when drug use is abruptly reduced or stopped after dependence has
  • developed. It is caused by the brain’s inability to immediately readjust after prolonged
  • neurochemical alterations.
  • General Features
  •  Symptoms are typically opposite to the drug’s acute effects.
  •  Withdrawal reinforces continued drug use through negative reinforcement, where taking
  • the drug alleviates withdrawal discomfort.

questions.question: Explain how the brain’s reward system contributes to the misuse of narcotic drugs.
questions.solution_html:
• drugs.
  • All addictive drugs stimulate the brain’smesolimbic dopamine pathway, also called thereward
  • circuit.
  • This pathway runs from theventral tegmental area (VTA)to thenucleus accumbens (NAc)and
  • connects with theamygdala, hippocampus, and prefrontal cortex.
  • Normally, this system releases moderate dopamine for natural rewards like food and social
  • bonding.
  • Addictive drugs, however, cause alarge, unnatural surge of dopamine, creating intense
  • pleasure and reinforcing drug use.
  • With repeated use, the brain learns to link the drug with reward, strengthening these pathways
  • and making drug-seeking compulsive.
  • Over time, natural rewards lose importance, and the drug becomes the main source of
  • motivation.

questions.question: Explain how awareness programmes support families and communities in preventing substance abuse.
questions.solution_html:
• preventing substance abuse.
  • Importance of Awareness in Prevention
  •  Awareness programs are important for preventing substance abuse.
  •  They teach people about the dangers and long-term effects of drugs and alcohol.
  •  Many individuals, especially young people, start using substances because of ignorance
  • peer pressure, or curiosity.
  •  These programs provide correct information about the physical, mental, and social harms
  • of addiction and help people make informed choices.
  •  Awareness programs also clear up myths, reduce stigma, and encourage healthy lifestyles.
  • Preventing substance abuse is more effective than treating it.
  • Targeting Vulnerable Populations
  •  Young adults, adolescents, and marginalized communities are particularly vulnerable to
  • substance abuse.
  •  Awareness programmes tailored to these groups can address specific risk factors such as
  • unemployment, academic stress, family issues, and lack of recreational activities.
  •  School and college-based campaigns, community outreach, and media-driven initiatives
  • can reach these populations early, fostering resilience and promoting coping strategies.
  •  When people understand the risks and recognize early warning signs, they are more likely
  • to seek help or avoid harmful substances altogether.
  • Reducing Health Burden and Social Costs
  •  Substance abuse leads to a cascade of health problems, including chronic diseases, mental
  • illness, and increased risk of accidents and violence.
  •  It also places a heavy burden on healthcare systems and law enforcement.
  •  Awareness programmes can reduce these costs by encouraging early intervention and
  • promoting rehabilitation.
  •  They also help families and communities understand how to support affected individuals
  • reducing isolation and improving recovery outcomes.
  •  In the long run, prevention through education is more cost-effective than managing the
  • consequences of addiction.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain natural narcotics and their medical implications.
questions.solution_html:
• Natural Narcotics
  • These are directly derived from the opium poppy plant (Papaver somniferum). The primary
  • natural narcotics include morphine, codeine, and thebaine. Morphine is the most potent and
  • widely used for severe pain relief, especially in post-surgical and cancer patients. Codeine is
  • milder and often used in cough syrups and mild painkillers. These substances act on opioid
  • receptors in the brain to reduce pain perception and induce sedation.
  • Morphine is a powerful opioid analgesic used to treat moderate to severe pain, but its strong
  • effects on the brain's reward system make it highly addictive and prone to misuse.
  • Morphine is widely used in clinical settings for acute and chronic pain management. It is
  • especially valuable in treating pain associated with surgery, trauma, cancer, and palliative
  • care. It can be administered orally, intravenously, subcutaneously, or via epidural routes
  • depending on the clinical need. In emergency medicine, morphine is also used to relieve pain
  • from myocardial infarction (heart attack) and to reduce anxiety
questions.final_answer: from myocardial infarction (heart attack) and to reduce anxiety
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain social stigma and discrimination faced by substance abusers.
questions.solution_html:
•  The social repercussions of substance abuse are profound and far-reaching.
  •  It often leads to strained relationships with family, friends, and colleagues due to
  • behavioural changes, dishonesty, and neglect of responsibilities.
  •  Substance abusers may isolate themselves or become aggressive, causing emotional
  • distress to those around them.
  •  In communities, drug abuse can contribute to increased crime rates, including theft
  • violence, and drug trafficking.
  •  Educational and professional achievements are frequently disrupted, as individuals may
  • drop out of school or lose their jobs.
  •  Social stigma and discrimination further marginalize users, making reintegration into
  • society difficult.
  •  These consequences not only affect the individual but also destabilize families and
  • communities.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the use of narcotic drugs in the treatment of diarrhoea.
questions.solution_html:
• Narcotics like loperamide and diphenoxylate are used to manage severe diarrhoea. These
  • drugs
  • slow intestinal motility by acting on opioid receptors in the gastrointestinal tract, allowing
  • more time for water absorption and reducing stool frequency.
questions.final_answer: more time for water absorption and reducing stool frequency
